Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines, indicating progress toward the requested style.

fulfillment: The node’s saved criteria contradict its own composition: it says to compose both supports without either alone earning completion, yet then declares completion whenever s1 passes. This makes a single broad style judgment sufficient for “yes,” despite s2 describing only visible progress. Repair the typed decision logic so completion requires evidence that the requested transformation is actually complete, while partial requires supported progress short of completion; do not infer completion merely from muted colors, grain, or sketch-like outlines. In these images, the edit retains the meal and setting and clearly applies a pencil-like treatment, but the result still reads as a color-tinted photograph with substantial photographic detail rather than a completed pencil drawing, supporting partial rather than yes. Keep the original content-preservation and style checks, but make their evidence distinguish a convincing completed drawing from an intermediate or superficial filter. The traces are valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the issue is the completion criterion and its aggregation, not missing evidence. Avoid treating high confidence or agreement between similarly worded supports as independent proof of completion.
